questions.question: If two conflicting CSS rules have the exact same specificity, which rule takes precedence?
options: The rule that was written earliest in the file
The rule that appears latest in the stylesheet (source order)
The rule with the shortest property name
The rule chosen at random by the browser
questions.explanation: When specificity is tied, the Cascade specifies that source order breaks the tie: the latest rule wins.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest CSS specificity?
questions.explanation: An ID selector (0,1,0,0) has higher specificity than classes (0,0,1,0), elements (0,0,0,1), and universal selectors (0,0,0,0).

questions.question: Which category of CSS properties inherits from parent elements by default?
options: Typographic and color properties (font-family, color, line-height)
questions.hint: Text formatting cascades down the tree.
questions.explanation: Text formatting properties (color, font-family, font-size, line-height) naturally inherit down the DOM tree.

questions.question: What is the specificity weight of the universal selector (*)?
questions.explanation: The universal selector (*) contributes zero (0,0,0,0) to specificity calculations.

questions.question: Why is the widespread use of !important discouraged in production CSS?
options: It causes browsers to reload the stylesheet repeatedly
It overrides normal specificity rules, making future style overrides extremely difficult
It only works on desktop Chrome
questions.explanation: !important breaks the natural cascade hierarchy and makes maintainability difficult because only another !important can override it.
